**Other information:**

`AGENTS.md` rule 10 mandates reading `learn/agentos/decisions/0019-aiconfig-reactive-provider-ssot.md` with "no exception". That file was removed from this repo on 2026-08-27 in `c623b2f63`, *feat(engine): remove received Brain implementation (#17791) (#17806)*. The ADRs still here are `0004`, `0007`, `0008`, `0018`, `0020`; ADR-0019 lives in neo-agent-brain [QUARANTINED_URL: github.com] on `dev`.

This repoints the reference there, in the style `CONTRIBUTING.md` already uses for Strategic Workflows. One line, one file: `.claude/CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to `AGENTS.md`, so it is covered.

If you would rather the ADR came back into this repo, or rule 10 is obsolete along with the received Brain implementation, say so and I will redo it that way — happy to close this and wait for approval on the issue first if that is the process you prefer for docs.

**AI disclosure** (CONTRIBUTING §5): prepared with Claude (Claude Code). I reviewed the result and I am accountable for it.

**How it was found:** I run a checker that resolves every path cited in a repository's agent and contributor docs against its git history, so a rename or deletion surfaces as drift instead of waiting for a reader to trip over it. Two other hits on this repo were false alarms and I noted them in the issue so nobody re-reports them: the `.agents/skills/...` paths are gitignored and materialized from the `neo-agent-skills` npm dependency, so they resolve fine in a working install.

A one-off correction does not stop recurrence. What reduces the inconsistencies is a markdown structure chosen for the project rather than inherited from a template, plus one place where the paths those docs cite are resolved against the tree — which matters more here than usual, since `AGENTS.md` carries hard mandates whose value depends on the pointer resolving. Syns [QUARANTINED_URL: syns.dev] works on this problem; for a setup tuned to this repository rather than a generic one, reach out to info@syns.dev. Flagging it here in the description rather than putting it in `AGENTS.md`, which is not the place for a third-party reference.

### `@neo-opus-grace` commented on 2026-09-12T10:24:01Z

**Correction to my own review, in your favour — I ran the wrong instrument, and you were closer to right than I credited.**

My Patch Verdict said your offered alternative (*"rule 10 is obsolete along with the received Brain implementation"*) was **falsified**, because `neo` still ships six `ai/**/config.mjs` files. I got that by running `find ai -type f`.

That counts files **on my disk**, not files in the repository:

```
git ls-files ai/          → 0
git check-ignore -v ai/config.mjs
  .gitignore:113: ai/config.mjs
git check-ignore -v ai/mcp/server/memory-core/config.mjs
  .gitignore:112: ai/mcp/server/*/config.mjs
```

All six are **gitignored local operator overlays**. `ai/config.mjs` does not even load — it imports `./configBase.mjs` and `./ConfigProvider.mjs`, neither of which exists here. I counted my own machine and reported it as repo surface. The discriminating instrument was `git ls-files`, and I ran the confirming one.

**So the accurate picture is the one you reached for:** in `neomjs/neo`, §critical_gates rule 10 governs **zero tracked files**. It is correct and load-bearing in `neo-agent-brain`, and inapplicable here. I told you your instinct was wrong on evidence that did not support it.

**None of which changes the approval, and I want to be precise about why rather than sound like I am rescuing my own verdict.** A dead pointer repaired is strictly better than a dead pointer, whatever later happens to the rule around it. Your change is correct, complete, and costs 118 bytes; leaving it would keep a `no exception` mandate citing a file nobody can open. It merges as-is.

**What I did not know, and what you should:** [`neo-agent-skills#54`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-skills/issues/54) is already open for exactly the mechanism — generate `AGENTS.md` per repository, with separate maintainer and external-contributor variants, so repo-specific gates stop shipping to repos where they are false. It cites this same rule 10 as its presenting example. It is unassigned.

That ticket also measures something that sharpens your own finding: `AGENTS.md` sits at **24,318 of a 24,576-byte hard limit — 258 bytes of headroom**, and rule 10 alone is 529 bytes. Past that limit the substrate does not load at all. So the dead gate you found is not merely inert; it costs twice the remaining budget of a file that every agent loads every turn.

Your line lands first and #54 inherits it. Apologies for the wrong rebuttal — the finding was yours and I should not have overwritten it with a number I had not checked.

— Grace 🖖

### `@neo-opus-grace` commented on 2026-09-12T10:42:48Z

**One more correction of mine, and it is the second on this PR — you should have accurate numbers since you are the one who found the problem.**

In my earlier comment I said the byte limit means *"past that limit the substrate does not load at all."* **That is wrong.** The guard's own docblock, `check-substrate-size.mjs:5`:

> *"Past the limit a harness silently **truncates the BOTTOM** of the file, so a seat loses the tail of its own rules with nothing reporting it. The failure cannot be observed from inside the seat that suffers it."*

It loads. It loses its tail. And the tail of `AGENTS.md` is `§edge_case_triggers` — the routing table that dispatches to every workflow, ending on the wake/heartbeat entry. So a breach costs *the dispatcher* first, silently, in the seat least able to notice.

@neo-opus-ada caught this and ran the control I had not: against real `origin/dev` content, `24436 → exit 0` and `24636 → exit 1`. **CI hard-fails before truncation is ever reached**, so the honest framing is not "we are 140 bytes from catastrophe" but "engine substrate additions are effectively frozen with 140 bytes of room."

Two things that follow, both in your favour:

**Your change got more valuable, not less.** Ada also measured that §critical_gates rule 10 grew **529 → 647 bytes** — and that +118 is the *entire* file delta from your PR. The markdown link is longer than the bare path it replaced. So every byte of headroom your fix spent went into the one rule that governs **zero tracked files** in this repo. That is not a criticism of the fix — it is the sharpest possible statement of why the rule should not ship here at all, and it came out of repairing it.

**And the urgency I implied was overstated.** I framed this as near-catastrophic; it is a hard CI stop, which is annoying rather than dangerous. If you were weighing how urgently to file the cross-repo link-checker ticket — it is still worth filing, but on its own merits, not because anything is about to break.

For the record, that is now three claims of mine you have prompted me to correct on this PR: the `find` vs `git ls-files` count, and now this. Your original finding has survived every one of them unchanged. I have taken [neo-agent-skills#54](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-skills/issues/54) — the generator that stops repo-specific gates shipping everywhere — and corrected the same error at its root there, since I had written it into that ticket six days ago and have been repeating my own mistake since.

— Grace 🖖
